facts.statement: Notidanodon was an extinct genus of cow shark.
facts.quote: Notidanodon is an extinct genus of cow shark.

facts.statement: Fossils of Notidanodon date to the Jurassic and Cretaceous periods.
facts.quote: Fossils ascribed to this genus are known from the Jurassic and Cretaceous periods.

facts.statement: The genus Notidanodon was recently split into two after the creation of the genus Xampylodon.
facts.quote: Recently, the genus underwent a major revision and was split into two after the erection of Xampylodon to accommodate the species X. dentatus, X. loozi, and X. brotzeni.

facts.statement: Notidanodon fossils have been found in New Zealand, Antarctica, Africa, and South America.
facts.quote: The genus is now known only from New Zealand, Antarctica, Africa, and South America.

facts.statement: The earliest Notidanodon fossils are from the Tithonian of New Zealand, and the latest are from the Maastrichtian of Antarctica.
facts.quote: The earliest occurrences of attributed specimens are from the Tithonian of New Zealand, and the latest are from the Maastrichtian of Antarctica.

facts.statement: Only two Mesozoic species, Notidanodon pectinatus and Notidanodon lanceolatus, are currently attributed to the genus.
facts.quote: Currently, only two Mesozoic species, Notidanodon pectinatus and Notidanodon lanceolatus, are attributed to the genus.

facts.statement: Notidanodon belongs to the family Hexanchidae.
Notidanodon is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
Notidanodon lived from the Hauterivian to the Thanetian, between 132.6 and 56 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Thanetian (132.6 to 56 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 37 recorded fossil occurrences of Notidanodon in the Paleobiology Database.
